before_introductions.detector_base: Seeklet spots things humans might otherwise have to find themselves. Its huge eyes turn pixels into patterns and patterns into guesses about what is there. Change the lighting, hide half an object, or show it something unlike its training data, though, and those impressive eyes can get impressively confused.
before_introductions.detector_disease: Pathogaze turns Seeklet's eyesight toward medicine. Some versions answer "Does this scan look suspicious?" while others locate or precisely outline abnormal tissue. Those are different AI tasks, and in healthcare a confident-looking mistake is still a mistake, so clinicians, validation, and explanation matter.
before_introductions.detector_pedestrian: Crowdseer doesn't just ask whether a person exists somewhere in an image. It has to find where they are. Rain, darkness, crowds, and the delivery truck blocking half the sidewalk all make that harder than your eyeballs would suggest.
before_introductions.detector_defect: Inspectra is the picky quality-control cousin. It can check products, shelves, components, or food for things that look wrong. Give it a night shift that looks nothing like its pristine training photos, though, and suddenly the expert inspector may be staring confidently at shadows.
before_introductions.anomaly_base: Quirkle's whole personality is "...that's weird." It learns what normal-ish behavior looks like and raises a tiny reptilian eyebrow when something wanders off-pattern. It doesn't necessarily know what happened or why. It only knows that this case deserves another look.
before_introductions.anomaly_fraud: Swindlisk hunts for transactions that don't smell right. A strange location, amount, or spending pattern might mean fraud, or it might mean you dared to go on vacation. Its job is usually to identify risk, not pronounce guilt.
before_introductions.anomaly_vitals: Beatling listens for the body getting out of rhythm. One unusual number may mean very little, so useful systems watch how measurements change over time and relative to context. Otherwise Beatling becomes the reptilian equivalent of a smoke detector screaming because you made toast.
before_introductions.anomaly_machine: Geargoyle hears the mechanical version of "that noise wasn't there yesterday." Changes in vibration, heat, or other sensor patterns can reveal trouble before equipment fails dramatically. The trick is learning the difference between dangerous weird and perfectly normal weird.
before_introductions.anomaly_network: Netnark is a tiny digital snitch. Strange login times, odd traffic bursts, or unusual connections make it suspicious, but Steve working from Japan at 3 a.m. is not automatically a cyberattack. Good anomaly detection tells humans what deserves investigation.
before_introductions.forecast_base: Forespirit peers into the future by studying the past. Trends, seasons, and context help it estimate what comes next, but it is not actually psychic. Pandemics, storms, and Beyoncé concerts remain formidable enemies of the forecasting arts.
before_introductions.forecast_patient: Wardwisp tries to see a hospital rush before it arrives. Predicting patient volume can help prepare beds, staff, and supplies, but historical utilization also reflects who could and could not access care in the past.
before_introductions.forecast_transit: Commutoracle sees rush hour coming. It combines old travel patterns with things like time, weather, and events to estimate future movement. Then somebody closes a road for construction and its crystal ball develops a stress rash.
before_introductions.forecast_stock: Coinjurer predicts what the shelves will need before customers arrive. Too much stock wastes money and too little means empty shelves. The fun wrinkle is that yesterday's forecast changed yesterday's inventory, which can influence the data used for tomorrow's forecast.
before_introductions.forecast_crowd: Gathergeist senses an incoming swarm of humans. Venues can use forecasts to prepare staffing, food, and safety resources, but crowds remain gloriously capable of ignoring smooth mathematical curves.
before_introductions.recommender_base: Suggestle studies a giant pile of choices and chirps, "THIS ONE. YOU WANT THIS ONE." Recommendations can reduce overload beautifully, but repeatedly feeding people what they already clicked can turn personalization into a very comfortable little tunnel.
before_introductions.recommender_product: Cartivore collects shiny products and pushes the promising ones toward you. One innocent lamp purchase may convince it that lamps are now your defining personality trait, because behavioral data is useful but not clairvoyant.
before_introductions.recommender_content: Reelure uses flashy plumage to tempt you toward the next song, movie, or article. The important question isn't just whether it predicts another click. It is whether more engagement is actually the outcome we wanted.
before_introductions.recommender_ai_curator: Muselect is Reelure with a museum key. Duke's Nasher Museum converted information about nearly 14,000 collection objects into machine-readable data for ChatGPT, which helped select artworks and create exhibition text and sequencing for an actual exhibition. The museum used the experiment to examine AI's usefulness and limitations in curatorial work.
before_introductions.recommender_learning: Curriquill wants to know what would help you learn next. It may offer another practice problem, a reading, or a different explanation, but students have motivations and misunderstandings that don't fit neatly into click histories.
before_introductions.recommender_adaptive_learning: Mentamorph changes its feathers as the learner changes. In EcoJourneys, the Friday Institute and collaborators added language-model capability that evaluates individual and group activity and provides tailored feedback during a science problem-solving game. That's personalized AI responding while learning is happening, not merely recommending the next video.
before_introductions.recommender_research: Referaptor swoops in carrying papers you didn't know you needed. NC State Libraries offers Keenious, an AI tool that analyzes writing or a text sample and recommends relevant scholarly publications. It can uncover literature beyond obvious keywords, but you still have to decide whether the papers are good evidence.
before_introductions.recommender_menu: Nibblet flits around the menu asking, "What sounds good today?" Preference prediction is useful for taste. Allergies and medical restrictions are different. Those belong in hard safety constraints, not "the bird thinks you'll probably be fine."
before_introductions.extractor_base: Scribbit gnaws through paperwork and stores the useful facts in its cheeks. Extracting a date, medication, or name is different from understanding an entire document, and a confidently extracted wrong fact can be more dangerous than a blank field.
before_introductions.extractor_medical: Clinink rummages through clinical notes for the facts humans need. "History of pneumonia," "possible pneumonia," and "no pneumonia" all contain the same tempting word, which is why context matters more than keyword hunting.
before_introductions.extractor_government: Bureaucritter bravely enters the paperwork maze so you don't have to. It converts boxes, scans, and forms into usable fields, but one misread digit can still transform helpful automation into an entirely new bureaucratic adventure.
before_introductions.extractor_research: Scholarat can chew through more papers than any reasonable human and drag useful facts back to the nest. Its advantage is scale, not magical truth. Anything it extracts still inherits the weaknesses of the source material.
before_introductions.extractor_history: Archivole burrows through whole archives instead of one document at a time. A Friday Institute project uses AI modeling software to help high-school history students investigate patterns across large collections of primary-source texts about redlining, patterns difficult to study one document at a time.
before_introductions.extractor_archive: Manusqueak turns old handwriting into searchable text. The farther a document gets from today's tidy digital fonts, the more every faded flourish becomes a tiny archaeological mystery.
before_introductions.extractor_specimen: Specimunk has graduated from old papers to old fish. The NC Museum of Natural Sciences holds about 1.5 million fish specimens, and UNC's Renaissance Computing Institute is working with the museum to reduce the time spent manually transferring handwritten specimen notes into electronic records using AI.
before_introductions.scheduler_base: Plancton swims through the problem of "too many things, not enough time." Unlike a forecaster, it doesn't merely predict what might happen. It chooses a plan. That means whoever defines "best" quietly defines what Plancton will optimize for.
before_introductions.scheduler_hospital: Wardray plays very high-stakes Tetris with beds, staff, equipment, and time. A mathematically efficient schedule can still be terrible if the objective forgot something important about actual humans.
before_introductions.scheduler_transit: Routeopus has eight metaphorical arms and all of them are holding a timetable. It coordinates vehicles, routes, and timing, asking not merely "Will traffic be bad?" but "Given that, what should we do?"
before_introductions.scheduler_transit_flow: Flowfin rides the current instead of merely planning it. GoDurham has experimented with AI-powered tools that process onboard GPS, schedule, and performance information to support transit priority and reduce travel time in heavy traffic. Durham Station is the gameplay anchor for this system-level example, not a claim that the AI exists only at that coordinate.
before_introductions.scheduler_ride_booking: Cabcrab takes reservations after the humans clock out. GoDurham documents an AI scheduler and calling system that can help eligible riders manage or book trips outside staffed reservation hours. This is conversational AI meeting a very practical scheduling job, where accessibility and an escape hatch to humans matter enormously.
before_introductions.scheduler_traffic_signal: Signalquid glows red, yellow, and green for a reason. Raleigh's 2026 pilot uses AI to turn real-time traffic-camera video into data that transportation staff can use to improve signal timing and safety. The city says the pilot does not store video or collect identifying information.
before_introductions.scheduler_workforce: Shiftshark circles the roster until every shift is covered. Good scheduling balances demand, skills, laws, and worker preferences. Bad scheduling treats humans like identical puzzle pieces.
before_introductions.scheduler_delivery: Parcelprawn answers the deceptively horrible question "Who delivers what, in what order, by which route?" A handful of stops produces a shocking number of possible plans, which is why optimization gets invited to the party.
before_introductions.generator_base: Purrrompt doesn't just choose an answer. It makes something new. New, however, does not mean true. Generative AI can produce brilliant work, bland mush, or exquisitely phrased nonsense with exactly the same confidence.
before_introductions.generator_learning: Learnx can draft explanations, questions, and activities faster than a teacher can open seventeen tabs. But sounding educational and actually helping someone understand are two very different achievements.
before_introductions.generator_lesson_planner: Planthera prowls the lesson-planning process beside the teacher. Friday Institute researchers had experienced elementary teachers use Gemini while planning phonics, fluency, and reading-comprehension lessons, studying not only the finished lesson but how teachers evaluated, revised, and rejected AI suggestions.
before_introductions.generator_conversational: Meowlogue turns generation into a conversation. It can answer, clarify, and sometimes use tools, but a friendly voice makes it remarkably easy to forget that fluent language is not the same thing as reliable knowledge.
before_introductions.generator_classroom_chatbot: Lecturlynx lets students look behind the chatbot curtain. Friday Institute researchers worked with middle- and high-school students to create, test, and revise language-model-powered chatbots, deliberately investigating hallucination, accuracy, trust, and how human design choices shape AI behavior.
before_introductions.generator_creative: Articlaw is the flashy cousin: pictures, stories, music, and other creative media on command. A convincing generated image tells you that a model can make convincing pixels, not that the thing pictured ever existed.
before_introductions.generator_document: Quillcat is less "write me a dragon poem" and more "please rewrite these 450 terrible descriptions before I perish." It excels at repetitive drafting when humans keep ownership of factual correctness.
before_introductions.generator_catalog: Catalogar is Quillcat with an actual library job. NC State Libraries used a GitHub Copilot agent powered by Claude Opus 4.6 to research and draft standardized descriptions for roughly 300 devices and 150 software titles, then had staff review the rewrites side-by-side before publication.
before_introductions.retriever_base: Searchound's job is gloriously dog-like: go find the thing and bring it back. Modern search can compare meaning instead of exact words, but mathematically similar is still only a guess at what you actually needed.
before_introductions.retriever_research: Labraquery noses through scholarly literature using more than exact keywords. That helps when your wording differs from the papers you're looking for, but first result remains a ranking decision, not a certificate of truth.
before_introductions.retriever_semantic_search: Semantiff understands the scent of an idea, not just its exact spelling. Duke Libraries documents academic-search tools that use AI to interpret natural-language queries, surface related concepts, and suggest relevant sources. Here AI isn't writing the scholarship. It is helping researchers find their way to it.
before_introductions.retriever_records: Dachshundex is long enough to crawl through the filing cabinet. It can find laws, permits, and public records more quickly, but finding a document that mentions your problem is very different from knowing what that document legally means.
before_introductions.retriever_knowledge: Cognicollie herds scattered institutional knowledge into one place. Policies, manuals, and reports become searchable by meaning, but if it retrieves the wrong document, the chatbot sitting behind it may produce a beautifully written answer to the wrong question.
before_introductions.retriever_product: Bargainbeagle can sniff out "comfortable black shoes for standing all day" without needing an exact product name. Semantic search makes shopping queries more human, but the order of results can still reflect business incentives as well as relevance.
